summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase workflow end-to-end for cipher-box phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings), then execute the resulting plans wave-by-wave, and additionally set up a parallel git worktree to begin phase 69 work independently.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 was fully planned (research → VALIDATION.md → D-07 scope decision → pattern mapping → REQUIREMENTS.md registration → 12 plans across 7 waves), passed plan-checker and all coverage gates, and execution began sequentially on the main tree; Wave 1 (SDK read-path ROT-07 gate) completed and was independently verified (296/296 tests passing); a separate worktree for phase 69 was created off origin/main; Wave 2 execution was just kicked off.

repo: GSD plan:pre hooks for a phase are resolved from a registry with `when` conditions; a UI capability hook only fires the plan-gate block if it actually appears in activeHooks — the lower-level ui-plan-gate check can report block:true even when no UI hook is active for the phase, and must be cross-checked before treating it as a real gate.

gsd-tools query commit reporting `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands is a recurring false negative (also seen in prior sessions) — always verify with `git log` before treating it as a real failure.
REQUIREMENTS.md requires three coordinated edits when registering new requirement IDs: the requirement section itself, traceability rows, and the coverage summary.

Worktree execution mode is decided by a base-check (#683 auto-degrade) plus `worktree.baseRef` (default resolves to `head` vs `fresh`) — executors forking from `origin/main` instead of live HEAD would miss any uncommitted-to-main planning docs (e.g. PLAN.md files), so baseRef must be verified before dispatching parallel worktree executors.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree executors need their own `pnpm install`, which is expensive per worktree; for phases with mostly single-plan waves, running sequential execution on the main tree (reusing installed node_modules) is more efficient and robust than driving multi-worktree wave orchestration.
The gap-analysis.plan-post advisory gate's parser can choke on control characters in the `rendered` field output — running the check directly bypasses this.

code.finding: Root folder resolve path (`resolvePublishedNode`/`ensureRootFolderState`) is now gated with `RotationHighWater.enforceResolved` as part of plan 68.2-01 (ROT-07 anti-rollback gate on reads, not just writes).
`dfsFindFolder` child-loop traversal is gated with `enforceResolved`, closing the read-path zero-gating gap identified in RESEARCH Pitfall 2.
Pre-existing write-path `enforceResolved` gate that the new read-path gates (lines 781, 913) were added alongside.

workflow: When `git fetch` fails in a sandboxed session (no network), it's safe to proceed with the existing local `origin/main` ref if it can be independently confirmed current (e.g. it matches the known fork-base of another recently-created branch).

For genuinely independent phase work, create a plain `git worktree add` off `origin/main` (not off the current feature branch) so the new worktree starts from a clean slate rather than inheriting unrelated planning commits — and verify the worktree afterward for accidental contamination.

When executing multi-wave plans, spot-check completed waves by independently re-running the acceptance tests rather than trusting the subagent's self-reported PLAN COMPLETE summary, especially for security-critical foundation waves.

friction: git fetch could not reach GitHub from the sandboxed session, requiring a workaround of trusting the existing local origin/main ref after independent verification.
The advisory gap-analysis.plan-post gate's output parser failed on control characters, requiring a manual direct check instead.

The gsd-tools commit helper reported a false-negative `commit_failed` twice in this session (once for VALIDATION.md/REQUIREMENTS.md commits, once for the plan 68.2-01 metadata commit), requiring manual git log verification each time.

Determining whether the UI capability plan-gate hook was actually active required careful inspection of raw JSON since a lower-level check reported block:true independent of whether the hook was truly active.
open_items: D-03's poll-invalidation leg lacks automated behavioral test coverage (only grep-level coverage in Plan 09) — logged as a todo at .planning/todos/pending/2026-07-06-d03-poll-invalidation-lacks-automated-coverage.md for follow-up after phase 68.2 completes.

Phase 69 (FUSE + WinFsp Rust integration) worktree is set up at cipher-box-phase69 but planning has not started — user still needs to run /gsd-discuss-phase 69 (recommended first due to an under-specified grant-root scope algorithm and an open FUSE delete-authority-model question), then /gsd-plan-phase 69 and /gsd-execute-phase 69 in a separate session.

Phase 69's design-mirroring dependency on 68.2 (mirroring the SDK-owned read-chain design on the Rust side) means 68.2's CONTEXT.md/RESEARCH.md should be manually copied or cross-referenced into the phase-69 worktree before/while planning phase 69.

Phase 68.2 execution is still in progress (Wave 2 of 7 just started; Waves 3-7 — write facade + desync e2e, web rewire + store collapse, off-path pockets, service deletion + grep gate, mirror revert + full web-e2e gate — remain).
